$comment: Where each fixture came from. Retrieved 2026-10-01 with no fal API key: nothing here is a response to a job this pack ran, and no fixture is a hand-written guess at fal's shape.

catalogue.json.source: GET https://api.fal.ai/v1/models?endpoint_id=<id>&expand=openapi-3.0, one call per endpoint (no key needed, rate-limited without one); the eight `models[]` entries concatenated in the order of models.json

result-pixal3d.json.source: the `examples` of the output schema inside catalogue.json (fal-ai/pixal3d: `model_glb`); the same value is the Example Response on https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/pixal3d/llms.txt, which omits the required `seed`

result-rodin-v25.json.source: the `examples` of the output schema inside catalogue.json (fal-ai/hyper3d/rodin/v2.5: `model_mesh` only; fal documents no sample for `textures`, `model_meshes` or `seed`)

result-meshy-v6.json.source: every field's `examples` entry in the output schema inside catalogue.json (fal-ai/meshy/v6/image-to-3d), assembled into one object

result-hunyuan-pro.json.source: every field's `examples` entry in the output schema inside catalogue.json (fal-ai/hunyuan-3d/v3.1/pro/image-to-3d), assembled into one object

result-hunyuan-part.json.source: the `examples` of the output schema inside catalogue.json (fal-ai/hunyuan-3d/v3.1/part: `result_files`)

result-hunyuan-smart-topology.json.source: every field's `examples` entry in the output schema inside catalogue.json (fal-ai/hunyuan-3d/v3.1/smart-topology); fal's own sample lists an .obj as `model_glb`, which is why files are classified by extension, not by key

pricing.json.source: the shape is the `prices[]` response of GET https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing (https://fal.ai/docs/platform-apis/v1/models/pricing.md, which needs a key); each endpoint's unit_price and unit are the `endpointBilling` of its fal page https://fal.ai/models/<endpoint>, which the pricing API is documented to report
